text:
> “Christ’s church does NOT continue outside mine.”

Didn't you just concede earlier that for approximately eighteen centuries Christ and the Holy Ghost saved, indwelt, and sanctified Christians? How can they do that without priesthood authority?

You've shifted your position only when it's convenient for you: you now define Christ’s Church by valid priesthood authority and now admit that no such Church existed anywhere for eighteen centuries. You cannot reduce your previous position to God privately influencing sincere individuals. You are holding both positions and deploying whichever one the objection calls for: the generous one when I press you on eighteen centuries of Christian faith, the exclusive one when I press you on where Christ's church was. Your position remains inconsistent.

Let's remind ourselves of one thing:

I am not the one making claims of exclusivity – you are. 

And that’s what makes my job so easy. Any powerful working of the Spirit through sacraments, miracles, visions and personal encounters of Jesus Christ making unbelievers confess Jesus Christ is Lord, any producing of the fruit of the Spirit, any tangible and visible experience of the blessings of the Gospel outside your church – which can only happen if apostolic authority exists outside it – proves the entire premise of your religion false. Just one.

> Restoration

From what I read in your responses, your restorationist position requires you to establish these propositions:
1. Perpetual replenishment: Christ required the apostolic office itself, not merely apostolic doctrine or ordinary Christian ministry, to be continuously replenished in a living governing quorum
2. Universal extinction: When the apostolic quorum disappeared, every Christian ministry including elders, deacons, overseers, etc. also became unauthorized
3. Authentic restoration: That universally extinguished authority was later restored through Joseph Smith.

Those are the missing premises you continually assume rather than prove. None of what you've offered so far supports any of those:
- Showing that Christ gave the original Church apostles does not establish all three
- Showing that corruption arose does not establish any of them

> This is an undisputed fact. Protestants believe the same thing, which is why they don’t claim authority

"undisputed" is a loaded description that you fail to back up.

Protestants reject your assumption that New Testament ministry operates through the LDS conception of priesthood authority.

Your reasoning is circular:
1. Valid Christian authority means priesthood authority.
2. Non-LDS churches lack priesthood authority.
3. Therefore, non-LDS churches lack valid Christian authority.

Here is the problem Clinton: again and again you import your theological framework and assume the theological priors of your church in order to support your positions.

> Ephesians 4

I concede that the aorist "Edoken" does not, by itself, prove that apostles ceased, but showing that the aorist does not prove cessation is not the same thing as proving perpetual replenishment.

Your inference is:
1. Christ continues equipping and building His Church until it reaches maturity
2. Apostles were among the gifts Christ gave for that purpose
3. Therefore, the apostolic office must remain continuously occupied in every generation

That conclusion does not follow from the grammar. "Mechri" marks the duration of the Church’s equipping and building up.

Even if I were to hypothetically grant that it does, NOWHERE in Ephesians 4 says that every instrument named in verse 11 must remain continuously instantiated in precisely the same institutional form. You make a logical jump from the continuation of Christ’s overall ministry to the uninterrupted continuation of every individual office.

Once again you have a far heavier burden of proof that your single reference cannot support. You have failed to prove scripturally using a contextualized and exhaustive exegesis your premises, and instead have to rely on a specific interpretation of a single set of verses to prove your premises -- an interpretation your teachers have taught you that cannot be deduced from the rest of the text.
- Ephesians 4 never says every apostolic vacancy must be filled
- Ephesians 4 never says apostles must constitute a perpetually replenished quorum
- Ephesians 4 never says every subordinate ministry becomes invalid without that quorum
- Ephesians 4 never says the office will universally disappear and require restoration centuries later

Your interpretation also presents a logical dilemma.
- You argue that the offices must continue “until we all attain unity,” but you simultaneously claim that the apostles disappeared for eighteen centuries.
- If "Mechri" guarantees the uninterrupted historical presence of living apostles, their eighteen-century absence contradicts your interpretation
- If apostasy can interrupt that presence, then "Mechri" does not prove uninterrupted institutional continuation

You must still prove separately that every office had to remain continuously occupied, that the loss of apostles invalidated every other ministry, and that restoration was the prescribed remedy.

Once again, none of those are supported in the text. You have only derived your conclusions by presupposing they are true from what little prescriptive evidence is in the text.

> Acts 1

Your use of Acts 1 uses a basic hermeneutical mistake: you take one narrated event and convert it into a universal ecclesiastical rule.

Biblical narrative can establish normative teaching, but description does not automatically equal prescription. You need an apostolic or Christic command, an authorial explanation, or a consistently repeated pattern showing that Luke intends the event to function that way.

Show me that.

Acts 1 gives a specific event grounded in specific prophetic fulfillment. Peter quotes: “Let his camp become desolate” and “Let another take his office” (Acts 1:20; Ps 69:25; 109:8). Matthias’s appointment fulfills a prophecy specifically applied to Judas.

Acts 12 then provides the obvious test case, which you still have not addressed. James the son of Zebedee, one of the Twelve, is killed. Luke records no replacement, no election, no prophetic appeal, and no restoration of the number Twelve. You have to make an assumption, informed by your theological priors, that this happened in order to support your premises. In the rulebook of the eisegesis you are using, you cannot prove any of your premises because you cannot fill the evidential absence with the very succession practice you are trying to prove.

If we use the authoritative Acts 1 narrative to dictate practice, how exactly does this text show that Peter derives the universal rule that whenever any apostle dies, another must take his office, when neither the equally authoritative Acts 12 nor the rest of the NT's treatment of continuing apostolic authority doesn't?

> apostle

Your appeal to Paul, Barnabas, James the Lord’s brother, Silas, and Timothy inconsistently shifts between:
1. The unique office of the Twelve
2. The use of "Apostolos" for commissioned messengers

If everyone called "Apostolos" possessed the identical office, keys, and governing position of the Twelve, then the New Testament Church did not have a governing Quorum of Twelve. It had an indefinite and expanding number of apostles.

But if the Twelve constituted a unique foundational body, then calling Barnabas or another commissioned messenger an “apostle” does not prove that vacancies within the Twelve were perpetually replenished. Again, you have to import a theological prior here to make the language fit and support your LDS viewpoint.

You're inconsistent here too: you appeal to the Twelve when you need governing keys, switch to the broader category when the Twelve’s eyewitness qualifications become inconvenient, and then use that broader category to prove perpetuity of the narrower office. That is equivocation. That is a confused, logically unsound line of reasoning.

> D&C 107

You can't use D&C 107 to establish the meaning of the New Testament without circularity.

Remember that we are debating the authority of LDS prophets to provide a restoration using Scripture. You cannot use the D&C to define the biblical office and then use that definition to authenticate the D&C.

Nor is it my burden to prove that modern LDS apostles have not privately seen Christ. You claim they are specially commissioned witnesses of the risen Lord; therefore, you bear the burden of authenticating that positive claim. A possible, private, or unreported appearance is not public evidence.

> apostolic authority does not continue without living apostles

You keep demanding that I show how apostolic authority continues without living apostles. What do we see in the New Testament?
- Nowhere in the text do the apostles transmit their unique foundational office to an endless succession of new apostles. To infer that they did is to import your theological priors into the text.
- They deposit their doctrine in the Church (Jude 1:3, 2 Thess 2:15, 1 Tim 6:20, Gal 1:8–9)
- They appoint elders to shepherd it (Acts 14:23, Acts 20:17, 28, Titus 1:5, 1 Peter 5:1–3)
- They command those elders to entrust apostolic doctrine to successive generations of qualified teachers (2 Tim 2:2, Titus 1:9, 2 Tim 1:13–14, Heb 13:7)

Acts 20 is significant because it shows what Paul actually instructed. I'm not claiming it conclusively proves that apostles could never be replaced, but what it does show is that the apostolic response to the apostles' own departure was to entrust the church to elders and the Word, not to command apostolic succession.
- Paul knows he is departing and that false teachers will arise: “I know that after my departure fierce wolves will come in among you” (Acts 20:29).
- Paul summons the elders of the church (v. 17), says the Holy Spirit made them overseers, commands them to shepherd the Church (v. 28), and then declares: “And now I commend you to God and to the word of his grace” (Acts 20:32).
- Paul’s prescribed defense against post-apostolic corruption is:
1. elders made overseers by the Holy Spirit
2. vigilant pastoral oversight
3. the apostolic Word entrusted to them

Look at what Paul does from Scripture:
- He doesn’t command them to replace him
- He doesn’t tell them to maintain a Quorum of Twelve
- He doesn’t say their commission will expire when the apostles die
- He commits the Church after his departure to God, to His Word, and to its elders

Paul gives the same pattern when his death is imminent: “The time of my departure has come” (2 Tim 4:6). What provision does he make? “What you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also” (2 Tim 2:2).

Paul --> Timothy --> faithful men --> others.

What is transmitted is the apostolic teaching, entrusted to qualified teachers. Paul does not tell Timothy he (Paul) needs to ordain a replacement apostle.

Titus receives the same instruction: “Appoint elders in every town as I directed you” (Titus 1:5). Those elders must: “hold firm to the trustworthy word as taught” (Titus 1:9).

Again, the normative pattern is qualified elders holding firmly to the apostolic Word already delivered, using it to teach the Church and refute error.

Peter teaches the same thing. Anticipating his death, he says: “I will make every effort so that after my departure you may be able at any time to recall these things” (2 Pet 1:15). Peter’s provision for believers after his departure is his enduring apostolic testimony and not a promise that another apostle will occupy his place.

He then addresses the ordinary ministers who will shepherd the Church until Christ returns: “I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder … shepherd the flock of God that is among you … And when the chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory” (1 Pet 5:1–4). Peter places elders under Christ, the Chief Shepherd, and expects them to shepherd the flock until Christ appears. He does not place them under a future succession of living apostles.

The scriptural pattern is demonstrably consistent across the wide breadth of epistles:
- Apostles and prophets lay the foundation (Eph 2:20).
- The apostolic faith is delivered “once for all” to the saints (Jude 3).
- Elders are appointed in every church (Acts 14:23; Titus 1:5).
- Elders guard the flock after the apostles’ departure (Acts 20:17–32).
- Apostolic teaching is entrusted to successive generations of faithful teachers (2 Tim 2:2).
- Scripture equips the man of God for every good work (2 Tim 3:16–17).
- Elders shepherd the Church until the Chief Shepherd returns (1 Pet 5:1–4).
- Christians obey their continuing church leaders (Heb 13:7, 17).

That's what's in the text.

> Universal Extinction

Even if the unique apostolic office ceased, it does not follow that every elder and congregation became invalid and you haven't defended that at all.

Where does Scripture say that the commissions of the elders appointed by the apostles expired when the last apostle died?

Where does Scripture teach that an overseer appointed by the Holy Spirit lost his authority merely because no apostle remained alive?

2 Thess 2 doesn't bridge the gap. The passage predicts rebellion, deception, and the man of lawlessness. It never says every Christian minister will lose authority, every ordinance becomes invalid, or that the Church will disappear until some restoration in the future.

You define “apostasy” as universal loss of authority, cite a passage predicting apostasy, and conclude that the passage predicts universal loss of authority. That is defining your conclusion into your premise.

> Hegesippus

Blindly painting my reply to you on Hegesippus merely as a "fallacy" without addressing its substance, or even proving it is one, is, quite frankly, lazy. I know you can do better.

Hegesippus testifies that heresies arose after the apostles. He does not say that every elder, bishop, baptism, and congregation everywhere lost authority.

You just replaced one claim with another without proving the new one:
Corruption entered the Church
--> Christ’s authorized Church universally ceased to exist.

This is not a sound argument.

> Acts 8

Acts 8 distinguishes Philip’s ministry from the apostles’  role in confirming the Samaritan mission, and does distinguish between Philip's ministry and the apostles' role. I am not disputing there is no distinction between different ministries in the early church. However, it does not predict universal priesthood extinction after the apostles' death.

None of your examples support your conclusion:
- Philip preached and baptized the Samaritans. Peter and John did not rebaptize them
- Cornelius’s exceptional reception of the Spirit authenticated Gentile inclusion
- The Samaritans were not rebaptized
- Acts never says Apollos was rebaptized
- The Ephesian disciples were different people who had received John’s preparatory baptism

Your conclusion that all authority died with the apostles still remains disconnected; it doesn’t follow from the text.

> The false lie of the Trinity is the very thing apostolic authority and prophets prevent

You presuppose that the Trinity is false, treat its historical formulation as evidence of apostasy, and then use that supposed apostasy as evidence that the Trinity is false. Calling it “the false lie of the Trinity” is merely preaching your conclusion. Saying something edgy like this may make you feel smug and good about yourself, but this is not an argument.

Same thing with baptism for the dead. 1 Corinthians 15:29 mentions people practicing something called baptism for the dead. Paul does not command the practice, explain its procedure, connect it with priesthood authority, or teach that dead Christians cannot enter the kingdom without LDS proxy ordinances. You assume that the mentioned practice was divinely authorized, assume that it meant what modern LDS theology says it means, and then call the entire system “biblical.”

Even worse, you’ve now exposed a fundamental inconsistency in how you apply your 2 tests of the absence of apostolic authority (serious error about God's nature and serious doctrinal division): because if applied to Brigham Young, going by the rules you’ve just established, that means that your own church had no authority in1852, because Adam-God is exactly the category of error your tests are designed to detect. This was a public, authoritative teaching about who God is, delivered by the President of your church, defended by his successors, and repudiated by that same church 124 years later. Whatever those two tests prove about the early church, they prove about Brigham Young. Either use this line of reasoning or don’t because it makes you look inconsistent.

> committed to rejecting that truth

Here's where things stand now, Clinton:
- You haven't derived the exact LDS conception of a Great Apostasy
- You haven't shown that apostasy means universal extinction (your Micah and 1 Samuel proof texts actually show the opposite)
- You inserted the LDS Great Apostasy into every decisive definition and then treated the conclusion as its own proof
- You haven't shown where the elders appointed by the apostles lost their commission
- You haven't reconciled an eighteen-century extinction with your interpretation of Ephesians 4
- None of these remain proved:
1. That the apostolic office universally disappeared
2. That the ministries established by the apostles consequently became invalid
3. That restoration rather than reform was necessary

All you've done is reproduce what your teachers want you to read in the text without thoroughly and unequivocally deriving it from the text itself. You assign LDS meanings to “apostles,” “authority,” “apostasy,” “Church,” and even “salvation,” read those meanings back into selected verses, and then announce that the verses prove Mormonism.

The Gospel of Jesus Christ did not need to be restored.

I heard about this study from 2009 on the radio just now. Could it perhaps explain why certain parts of the third world are the way they are? 🤔 

Fascinating possibilities. From the article: 

"People are unconsciously fairer and more generous when they are in clean-smelling environments, according to a soon-to-be published study led by a Brigham Young University professor.

The research found a dramatic improvement in ethical behavior with just a few spritzes of citrus-scented Windex.

Katie Liljenquist, assistant professor of organizational leadership at BYU's Marriott School of Management, is the lead author on the piece in a forthcoming issue of Psychological Science. Co-authors are Chen-Bo Zhong of the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management and Adam Galinsky of the Kellogg School of Management at Northwestern University.

The researchers see implications for workplaces, retail stores and other organizations that have relied on traditional surveillance and security measures to enforce rules.

"Companies often employ heavy-handed interventions to regulate conduct, but they can be costly or oppressive," said Liljenquist, whose office smells quite average. "This is a very simple, unobtrusive way to promote ethical behavior."

Perhaps the findings could be applied at home, too, Liljenquist said with a smile. "Could be that getting our kids to clean up their rooms might help them clean up their acts, too."

The study titled "The Smell of Virtue" was unusually simple and conclusive. Participants engaged in several tasks, the only difference being that some worked in unscented rooms, while others worked in rooms freshly spritzed with Windex.

The first experiment evaluated fairness.

As a test of whether clean scents would enhance reciprocity, participants played a classic "trust game." Subjects received $12 of real money (allegedly sent by an anonymous partner in another room). They had to decide how much of it to either keep or return to their partners who had trusted them to divide it fairly. Subjects in clean-scented rooms were less likely to exploit the trust of their partners, returning a significantly higher share of the money.

The average amount of cash given back by the people in the "normal" room was $2.81. But the people in the clean-scented room gave back an average of $5.33.
The second experiment evaluated whether clean scents would encourage charitable behavior.

Subjects indicated their interest in volunteering with a campus organization for a Habitat for Humanity service project and their interest in donating funds to the cause.

Participants surveyed in a Windex-ed room were significantly more interested in volunteering (4.21 on a 7-point scale) than those in a normal room (3.29).
22 percent of Windex-ed room participants said they'd like to donate money, compared to only 6 percent of those in a normal room.
Follow-up questions confirmed that participants didn't notice the scent in the room and that their mood at the time of the experiment didn't affect the outcomes.

"Basically, our study shows that morality and cleanliness can go hand-in-hand," said Galinsky of the Kellogg School. "Researchers have known for years that scents play an active role in reviving positive or negative experiences. Now, our research can offer more insight into the links between people's charitable actions and their surroundings."

While this study examined the influence of the physical environment on morality, Zhong and Liljenquist previously published work that demonstrated an intimate link between morality and physical cleanliness. Their 2006 paper in Science reported that transgressions activated a desire to be physically cleansed.

Liljenquist is now researching how perceptions of cleanliness shape our impressions of people and organizations. "The data tell a compelling story about how much we rely upon cleanliness cues to make a wide range of judgments about others," she said."

text:
Culture Clash and Fatima's Ass

Me and my friend Bob were just hanging out one night. We had just finished off a burger and fries at an In-N-Out and we were walking over to the multiplex to see if something interesting might be playing. As we were crossing the parking lot, a large swarthy guy with a curly deep black beard and wearing a tight black Tee accentuating his well built physique, and painted on black jeans accentuating the rest, walked by us. At his side was a beautiful, well structured, dark woman in clothing complementing her companion's.

Now, what happened next that triggered off the guy (we later got his name to be Abdul and the striking young lady's, Fatima) was not initially clear.

But it seemed that as Bob and I crossed paths with Abdul and Fatima, that Abdul thought he had caught Bob take, for just a microsecond or two, too long a glance at Fatima's well displayed ass.

Even had Bob copped such a glance, in America such a thing is no big deal, and can even be taken as a compliment if done in the right spirit. And I am sure this was Bob's spirit, because Bob grew up admiring some very fine asses in the beaches and towns of Southern, California, and it never drew more than a smile.

Not so much in the throwback country Abdul and Fatima hailed from. In Abdul's hometown, if you wanted to appreciate some good ass, it would be safer to look at the behind of Abdul's donkey, than that of his girlfriend. Maybe that is why they cover up their women so thoroughly back there, just to prevent what was about to take place here.

Abdul stopped in front of Bob and myself, blocking our way to the multiplex, which was also their destination. Abdul stared down at Bob and growled in a kind of gurgling grating voice, "Apologize to my woman!"

Bob was the first to get it together enough to ask, while holding back a tremor, "what am I apologizing for?" In the back of his mind he remembered the fleeting glance at the ass of Fatima, but since, as mentioned, Bob had grown up looking at innumerable fine asses.on the beaches of Orange County, he really had no idea of what he might have done to insult this Fatima woman, since at the time of his coup d'oeil at Fatima's ass, Bob and I were talking about the line on the Dodgers game that night and whether Shohei was well enough to pitch.

The problem quickly defined itself, in that Abdul had felt ashamed to say out loud, that in his presence, while with Fatima, another man had insulted his girlfriend by looking with lust at her ass.

So after a few, "Apologize!!"/"For what?"/"You know for what!!"/"No, I don't." 's, after a few of these, then came the threat.

And Abdul did not hold back. Nearly breathing fire, he screamed, "You either apologize or I will cut off your head!”

Now, this may have been an empty threat, however, since Fatima made not even the slightest effort to calm him down (and even though she likely had no idea that Bob had glanced at her ass), Bob and I had to take into consideration that Abdul might have a few heads on pikes in his backyard back home.

Since Bob had just begun to noticeably tremble, I decided it might be a good time to step in (before Abdul pulled out a knife from a scabbard), and use whatever skills I had picked up in a college debating class.

"Uh, Mr. Abdul, sir, maybe there is something short of cutting off my friend's head that might make you just as happy, because in the end, we do want you to be happy."
To which he replied, "Okay, maybe I cut off your head.",
To which I replied, "Well, no, HaH, I'll take that in the spirit, and not in the reality with which it was meant. So let's think of something a bit less than decapitation because, well because that is so final."

To which Abdul, softening up just a bit said, "Ok, how about I cut off his balls?"

"Ok, well, see there, now we have made some progress and have found something that might make you just as happy as cutting off mine or Bob's heads. But perhaps, we could find something a little less likely to ruin Bob 's life than cutting off his balls, because I know for a fact that Bob would like to have children."

Now, Abdul seemed to calm a bit, and Fatima began whispering in his ear. Finally, Abdul said with a serious smile, "Ok, my friends, we take your first borns."

Now, as radical as that sounded at first, Bob and I agreed that it surpassed the previous two offers, and, at any rate we did not know how enforceable such an agreement might be here in America. Abdul took our addresses and said he would get in touch.

A few days later Abdul and Fatima showed up with a document from some Sharia court signing over our first borns when they might become available. Since Bob and I were not even yet married, we thought it a bit of a lark signing a Sharia court document as such.

Years later, after we graduated, Bob and I remained close friends, attending and betting on Dodgers games. We stayed in the same town and set up ourselves in business in our chosen fields. We married and found our wives pregnant at about the same time. Being Christian, Bob, myself and our wives decided against ultrasounds before delivery and trusted in our Lord to give us the children He thought we needed.
Bob’s wife delivered a trisomy 21 boy and my wife delivered a few days later, a beautiful girl, but with tetralogy of Fallot.

Unbeknownst to us, in a nearby town had settled a large immigrant population. One day, soon after our children were born, Abdul and Fatima showed up at our doors with papers signed by some Sharia officials from the nearby town, assigning the rights adoption of our children to Abdul and Fatima. We shielded our wives from the insanity the best we could, but all was resolved when we explained the nature of our special children to Abdul and Fatima. The Sharia papers were torn up and we never heard from Abdul or Fatima again, as we lovingly raised our special children.

text:
Sports betting is not easy as some like to think. I see cappers all the time say, “let me go cap the board and I’ll be back”. They come back two hours later with 5 picks lol. I wish I were that good. 

I almost never bet much the first few weeks in CFB, just to give myself time to see the teams. I would also not make my POW pick on any of the radio shows I was on until the NFL started. But I would sit and watch games all day, and the ones I would miss, I would watch later. It is not like that for me now. 

I didn’t watch one play from my Gators. I didn’t watch one play from the Clemson game. I watched about 2 quarters from the UCLA game. That was it for the entire day. 

I have been offered so many times to come back and continue making picks. From both old players of mine, and radio show host. Which is also why I have thrown out some unofficial picks here and there. I have turned them down, because I just don’t have the desire any longer. The more I try to get into it, the more I realize it is not there for me. 

I truly believe that once you lose your desire for something, no matter how many times you try to go back, you will not be able to put forth 100%. And that’s not what I’m about. That’s where I am and will probably stay. 

I wish everyone out there luck all season long, even the ones I have given grief to over time. I will always pull for the players over the book. But for me, I am done. 

And it probably will not be worth the $4 I spent to write this lol, but I wanted to be clear. Take care!!!

text:
When they start a war it's Jihad, when they lose it becomes genocide. Lol. 

I fail to see where Israel is the problem. Arab and Palestinian leaders rejected every major formal two-state offer while launching or sustaining waves of attacks on Jewish and Israeli civilians. Egypt, Jordan, the UAE, Bahrain, and Morocco signed peace or normalization agreements with Israel and honor them; peace holds. If Israel wanted to eradicate a people or place it would have happened. It has not.

Rejected offers  
1937 Peel Commission: British partition into small Jewish state and larger Arab state. Arab Higher Committee and Mufti Haj Amin al-Husseini rejected any Jewish state. Jews accepted in principle.  
1947 UN Partition Plan Res 181: Jewish and Arab states. Arab leadership rejected it and launched war. Jews accepted.  
1967 post-Six-Day War: Israel offered land-for-peace under UN 242. Arab League Khartoum replied with three no’s: no peace, no recognition, no negotiation.  
2000 Camp David: Clinton and Barak offered Palestinian state on roughly 91-95 percent of West Bank plus all Gaza, land swaps, shared Jerusalem arrangements. Arafat rejected with no counter-offer. Second Intifada followed.  
2000-2001 Clinton Parameters and Taba: refined offer near 97 percent with swaps. Arafat effectively rejected.  
2005 Gaza Disengagement: Sharon unilaterally withdrew all settlers and forces from Gaza and some northern West Bank settlements. PA under Abbas took control. Hamas later seized Gaza; rockets and rejectionism continued.  
2008 Olmert offer: roughly 93-94 percent of West Bank with 1:1 land swaps, all Gaza, shared Jerusalem holy basin, limited refugee return. Abbas did not accept.  
2020 Trump Peace to Prosperity: Palestinian state with land swaps, $50B economic package, security conditions. Abbas and PA rejected it outright.  
Oslo 1993 created the PA and a process; final-status talks collapsed amid violence and rejections. Bush Roadmap and Kerry talks stalled without signed deals.

Key attacks  
1920 Nebi Musa riots: Arab mobs kill Jews in Jerusalem.  
1921 Jaffa riots: dozens of Jews killed.  
1929 Hebron and Safed massacres: 133-plus Jews slaughtered; Jewish communities erased in Hebron.  
1936-1939 Arab Revolt: hundreds of Jews killed in attacks on settlements, roads, and civilians.  
1947-1949: after rejecting partition, civil war attacks plus invasion by Arab states; thousands of Jews killed.  
1950s: fedayeen raids from Gaza/Egypt and Jordan kill hundreds of Israeli civilians.  
1960s-1970s PLO terrorism including airplane hijackings and bombings. 1972 Munich Olympics: Black September takes Israeli athletes hostage; 11 murdered. Ma’alot school massacre 1974. Coastal Road bus massacre 1978.  
First Intifada 1987-1993: stabbings, shootings, Molotovs; roughly 200 Israelis killed.  
Second Intifada 2000-2005: suicide bombings and shootings; over 1,000 Israelis killed.  
Post-2005 Gaza: thousands of rockets and mortars from Hamas and Islamic Jihad; major rounds 2008-09, 2012, 2014, 2021. Knife and car-ramming waves from 2015.  
October 7 2023: Hamas-led assault kills roughly 1,200 Israelis, mostly civilians, takes hostages, includes mass rape and atrocities.

Palestinian groups including PLO factions, Hamas, and Islamic Jihad have carried out or claimed these campaigns against Jewish and Israeli civilians from the Mandate era to the present.

text:
🌧️ తెలుగు రాష్ట్రాల వర్షాల అప్‌డేట్ — సెప్టెంబర్ 6 - సెప్టెంబర్ మొదటి వారం “లోటు పూడ్చే విస్తృత వర్షాలు” పడే అవకాశం ఇప్పడు కనిపించడం లేదు. ముఖ్యంగా APలో పరిస్థితి తీవ్రమే; తెలంగాణలోనూ deficit మళ్లీ పెరుగుతోంది. ఇప్పుడు ఒక్కో isolated shower కాదు—కొన్ని రోజుల పాటు విస్తృతంగా, సమానంగా కురిసే వర్షాలే పంటలకు, శ్రీశైలం వంటి జలాశయాలకు అవసరం. 

🌧️ ముందున్న వారం కూడా పెద్దగా ఆశాజనకంగా లేదు. IMD సెప్టెంబర్ 6–11 మధ్య AP, Rayalaseema, Telanganaలో ప్రధానంగా isolated to scattered rainfall మాత్రమే అంచనా వేసింది.

తెలంగాణకు సెప్టెంబర్ 6 నుంచి 11 వరకు isolated light to moderate rain మాత్రమే; heavy-rain warning లేదు. APలో సెప్టెంబర్ 4–10 వారానికి Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema రెండింటిలోనూ rainfall Deficientగా ఉండే అవకాశం ఉందని IMD Extended Range Forecast చెబుతోంది. 

The Karnataka government has already declared drought-hit mandals. However, the Andhra Pradesh and Telangana governments are yet to take a decision on declaring drought-affected areas.
Even in the acreage already cultivated, crops are showing poor and stunted growth due to prolonged moisture stress. Rains at this stage may offer some relief, but crop recovery and yields are likely to remain limited. If the rains fail again, the situation could turn disastrous, with farmers at risk of losing even the standing crops.

ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్: తాజా IMD cumulative data ప్రకారం జూన్ 1–సెప్టెంబర్ 2 మధ్య రాష్ట్రంలో 204.8 mm వర్షం మాత్రమే నమోదైంది; సాధారణం 378.6 mm. అంటే 46% లోటు. అంతకంటే ఆందోళనకరం—ఆగస్టు 27–సెప్టెంబర్ 2 వారంలో సాధారణ 31.9 mmకు బదులు కేవలం 3.6 mm, అంటే 89% weekly deficit; 26 జిల్లాల్లో 25 జిల్లాలు ‘Large Deficient’ కేటగిరీలో ఉన్నాయి. 

తాజాగా పూర్తిగా అందుబాటులో ఉన్న 24 గంటల IMD observationలో కూడా Monsoon Coastal AP, Rayalaseemaలో Weakగానే ఉంది. చిత్తూరు, పలసముద్రంలో సుమారు 3 cm, కుకునూరు, బలిజిపేటలో 2 cm వరకు వర్షం నమోదైనా, రాష్ట్రవ్యాప్తంగా వర్షాలు ఒకటి రెండు ప్రాంతాలకే పరిమితమయ్యాయి; భారీ వర్షం ఎక్కడా నమోదు కాలేదు. 

తెలంగాణ: తాజా IMD ఆధారిత cumulative figures ప్రకారం రాష్ట్ర Seasonal Rainfall Deficit సుమారు 21% కు చేరింది. ఆగస్టు 28 నాటికే 16 జిల్లాలు deficient categoryలో ఉండగా, హనుమకొండ −45%, వరంగల్ −43%, జనగామ,−40% తో తీవ్రంగా వెనుకబడ్డాయి; సెప్టెంబర్ ప్రారంభంలో రాష్ట్ర సగటు లోటు మరింత పెరిగింది. 

💧 జలాశయాలపై ప్రభావం: శ్రీశైలం పరిస్థితి ప్రత్యేకంగా ఆందోళనకరం. సెప్టెంబర్ 5 నాటికి కొత్త inflows దాదాపు లేకపోవడంతో storage సుమారు 139 TMCకు తగ్గింది. సెప్టెంబర్‌లో upstream catchmentsలో మంచి వర్షాలు రాకపోతే, releases కొనసాగుతున్న కొద్దీ నిల్వలు ఇంకా తగ్గే ప్రమాదం ఉంది. 

🌾 వ్యవసాయం: నీటి కొరత ప్రభావం ఇప్పటికే sowing patternలో కనిపిస్తోంది. గత ఏడాదితో పోలిస్తే APలో paddy acreage 1.26 లక్షల హెక్టార్లు, Telanganaలో 2.45 లక్షల హెక్టార్లు తక్కువగా నమోదైంది; APలో pulses వైపు కొంత shift కనిపిస్తోంది.

text:
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has received
17 bids for the 160-km Rameshwar-Paradip greenfield coastal highway in Odisha,
with 10 bidders submitting offers for the Rameshwar-Konark package and seven
for the Konark-Paradip package. The INR 8,300.79 crore project was approved by
the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs in June and will be implemented under
the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM). The 79.4-km Rameshwar-Konark section will be a
four-lane access-controlled highway, while the 80.7-km Konark-Paradip stretch
will have two lanes with paved shoulders. The corridor is designed for a speed
of 100 kmph and is expected to reduce travel time between Rameshwar and Paradip
by around 2.5 hours while improving access to Puri, Konark, Paradip Port and
the upcoming Puri International Airport.

Feasibility & Technical Risk Evaluation

1. Cheyyur (Chengalpattu District) — 

Status: Unviable / High Rejection Risk
 Airspace & Defense Conflict (Primary Hard Stop):

Kalpakkam Atomic Power Station: Located ~35 km north. Commercial holding patterns, approach vectors, and missed-approach procedures run the risk of encroaching on restricted nuclear infrastructure airspace.

Tambaram Air Force Station: Standard Instrument Departure (SID) and Arrival (STAR) routes for Cheyyur overlap with military air traffic control (ATC) zones, which typically triggers objections from the Ministry of Defence.

Geographic & Connectivity Disadvantage:
 Situated ~100 km south of central Chennai.
 Lacks a high-density urban or industrial passenger catchment between Kilambakkam/Kovalam and the site.
 Metro extension plans are not economically viable over this distance, requiring massive capital expenditure for new greenfield expressways connecting to Madurantakam and the ECR.

Environmental Constraints:
Proximity to the Odiyur Lake backwaters and the Kazhuveli bird sanctuary/wetland ecosystem creates severe vulnerabilities under Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) rules and Union Environment Ministry (MoEFCC) clearances.

2. Gummidipoondi / Manellore (Tiruvallur District) — Status: High Risk / Dead on Arrival
 ISRO & Border Airspace Conflicts (Primary Hard Stop):
 Sriharikota (SDSC SHAR): Located ~35 km northeast. ISRO enforces active Danger/Restricted Airspace Zones (VOD 174) for rocket launch trajectories. Commercial flight paths cannot operate safely near active rocket launching corridors.

Interstate Coordination: Located ~13 km from the Andhra Pradesh border. Flight approaches and holding stacks would constantly cross into neighboring state airspace, complicating ATC authority and regulatory jurisdiction.
 Ecological & Wetland Vulnerability:
Adjacent to the Pulicat Lake lagoon system (India's second-largest brackish water lagoon).
 Constructing a multi-runway airport on coastal mudflats and low-lying floodplains would create significant flooding risks and face litigation under CRZ regulations.

Land Parcel Fragmentation:
 While the western inland corridor (toward Uthukkottai) offers dry scrubland, the eastern Gummidipoondi pocket consists of fragmented private agricultural plots (cultivating paddy, groundnut, and watermelon) and rural habitations like Soorapundi and Pallavada.

Acquiring 3,000–4,000 acres of contiguous land requires acquiring active farmland rather than vacant government land, risking the same local community resistance that halted Parandur.

Summary:

While Gummidipoondi offers better alignment with northern industrial hubs like Sri City and the CPRR corridor, it faces severe operational roadblocks from ISRO's Sriharikota launch clearances and Pulicat Lake environmental protections.

Conversely, Cheyyur avoids border conflicts but fails on basic aviation economics due to its 100 km distance from Chennai and proximity to defense/nuclear restriction zones. Both shortlisted locations present severe site-selection constraints during pre-feasibility analysis.

I fail to see where Israel is the problem. Arab and Palestinian leaders rejected every major formal two-state offer while launching or sustaining waves of attacks on Jewish and Israeli civilians. Egypt, Jordan, the UAE, Bahrain, and Morocco signed peace or normalization agreements with Israel and honor them; peace holds. If Israel wanted to eradicate a people or place it would have happened. It has not.

Rejected offers  
1937 Peel Commission: British partition into small Jewish state and larger Arab state. Arab Higher Committee and Mufti Haj Amin al-Husseini rejected any Jewish state. Jews accepted in principle.  
1947 UN Partition Plan Res 181: Jewish and Arab states. Arab leadership rejected it and launched war. Jews accepted.  
1967 post-Six-Day War: Israel offered land-for-peace under UN 242. Arab League Khartoum replied with three no’s: no peace, no recognition, no negotiation.  
2000 Camp David: Clinton and Barak offered Palestinian state on roughly 91-95 percent of West Bank plus all Gaza, land swaps, shared Jerusalem arrangements. Arafat rejected with no counter-offer. Second Intifada followed.  
2000-2001 Clinton Parameters and Taba: refined offer near 97 percent with swaps. Arafat effectively rejected.  
2005 Gaza Disengagement: Sharon unilaterally withdrew all settlers and forces from Gaza and some northern West Bank settlements. PA under Abbas took control. Hamas later seized Gaza; rockets and rejectionism continued.  
2008 Olmert offer: roughly 93-94 percent of West Bank with 1:1 land swaps, all Gaza, shared Jerusalem holy basin, limited refugee return. Abbas did not accept.  
2020 Trump Peace to Prosperity: Palestinian state with land swaps, $50B economic package, security conditions. Abbas and PA rejected it outright.  
Oslo 1993 created the PA and a process; final-status talks collapsed amid violence and rejections. Bush Roadmap and Kerry talks stalled without signed deals.

Key attacks  
1920 Nebi Musa riots: Arab mobs kill Jews in Jerusalem.  
1921 Jaffa riots: dozens of Jews killed.  
1929 Hebron and Safed massacres: 133-plus Jews slaughtered; Jewish communities erased in Hebron.  
1936-1939 Arab Revolt: hundreds of Jews killed in attacks on settlements, roads, and civilians.  
1947-1949: after rejecting partition, civil war attacks plus invasion by Arab states; thousands of Jews killed.  
1950s: fedayeen raids from Gaza/Egypt and Jordan kill hundreds of Israeli civilians.  
1960s-1970s PLO terrorism including airplane hijackings and bombings. 1972 Munich Olympics: Black September takes Israeli athletes hostage; 11 murdered. Ma’alot school massacre 1974. Coastal Road bus massacre 1978.  
First Intifada 1987-1993: stabbings, shootings, Molotovs; roughly 200 Israelis killed.  
Second Intifada 2000-2005: suicide bombings and shootings; over 1,000 Israelis killed.  
Post-2005 Gaza: thousands of rockets and mortars from Hamas and Islamic Jihad; major rounds 2008-09, 2012, 2014, 2021. Knife and car-ramming waves from 2015.  
October 7 2023: Hamas-led assault kills roughly 1,200 Israelis, mostly civilians, takes hostages, includes mass rape and atrocities.

Palestinian groups including PLO factions, Hamas, and Islamic Jihad have carried out or claimed these campaigns against Jewish and Israeli civilians from the Mandate era to the present.

text:
Prologue: Professor B.S.
Professor B.S. suffered from eternal insomnia. He sat before his television screen, far too alert.
3:21. 
An interesting hour. Even more so when read in reverse. A basketball game murmured in the background, entirely irrelevant.
B.S. was contemplating the critical ethics of eating during a lecture. Not the students eating; that was perfectly legitimate in his eyes. He was thinking about the lecturer eating, mid-presentation. Nothing heavy, like beef and potatoes. Something light. A pleasant little salad. Perhaps a can of something carbonated on the side. But the students might take offense. The pretentious ones would likely file a complaint with the faculty.
Ridiculous. It’s for their own benefit, B.S. mused. 
It would allow him to survive the mid-lecture hypoglycemia and bring the entire performance to a crescendo.
Perhaps he could bring in a patient while he was at it. Well, at least an actor. He could demonstrate meningeal signs on them - bend the neck until they screamed their soul out in pain.
Unpleasant.
Meningitis is undeniably unpleasant. Fortunately, only the actor must suffer.
Professor B.S. considered breaking his routine tomorrow to perform a ward round. A 'Peacock Walk,' just to remind everyone he was still among the living. Perhaps he would bark at someone regarding a botched chest X-ray interpretation, or, more amusingly, offer a rare word of praise to the department’s most incompetent resident. It was always good for a laugh.
The mere thought caused a twitch in his left flank. Or his right. Or both. Dealing with the actual practice of medicine was a dangerous business. Too demanding. Better to stick to lectures and remain entombed in his office. The air conditioning was sublime this time of year. Airy weather.
It was already four in the morning. Not good; sleep was no longer an option. Better to get dressed and brew some coffee. The morning would arrive soon enough.
*
Chapter 1 – Beep. Beep. Beep.
Beep. Beep. Beep.
White noise.
Beep. Beep. Beep.
White noise.
Dr. Eran Datner, the miserable resident on duty in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) at 'Sharona', glanced at his watch. 3:23. A digital watch. A toy for the new generation. He disliked the time staring back at him, something too symmetrical about it. Either too early to get up or far too late.
In any case, he wondered why he had woken up. The background drone of the monitors was a poor excuse. It was barely audible from behind the on-call room door in the NICU. It must be something else.
Ring. Ring. Ring.
The phone. The nurse Susan. Susan Schell.
That never meant anything good.
That American only spoke up to rant about vaccines or bark about resuscitation.
Resuscitation.
He leapt out of bed, nearly forgetting to put on his shoes, and bolted from the room. His thinning hair was disheveled, and he was wholly dazed and bewildered. He did not know what awaited him.
*
Datner nearly stumbled over the nurses' desk before truly opening his eyes. He felt sour. Like a lemon squeezed into a margarita that had sat in the sun for far too long.
He knew what he had to do.
Too late.
Washing his face now would make the nurses look at him strangely. Combing his hair was out of the question; he had never owned a comb (he knew he did not have much to comb anyway). It was time for action.
Room 11.
The resuscitation in Room 11.
Susan had said it explicitly, that unhinged American from hell.
Too harsh. Just an unhinged American, then. Still tough, though. American, the harshest curse of all.
Resuscitation.
He pulled back the curtain of Room 11.
*
A large incubator. Transparent. Horribly generic.
The baby was unmistakably blue.
It had a name, but no one cared about that at this stage. At this stage, it wasn't even clear what the baby’s sex was. A few things were clear to Datner now. The monitor above the incubator showed a low oxygen saturation of 76%, and the baby looked distinctly blue.
The pulse and blood pressure were not being read by the monitor, and there were too many nurses around the small incubator. At least three nurses. At least one of them was Susan Schell. That couldn't be good.
Worst of all, the incubator had not yet been opened. That really annoyed him.
He pushed his way past the flustered nurses, opened the incubator, and shouted at Susan - "The Ambu, now." He began ventilating. 'Not too hard,' he recalled the advice of his old mentor, Prof. B.S., 'Gently, so you don’t burst the baby’s lungs.'
The lungs, surprisingly, did not resist at all. The air pushed by the Ambu flowed easily into the small body, which gradually turned pinker and pinker.
"What are the blood pressure and pulse?" Datner called out into the air, stifling a small smile at the saturation rising to 99%. Even better than 100, better symmetry. The sound the monitor emitted became much more tolerable. Almost melodic. Harmonic. The Beach Boys at their peak. God Only Knows.
"Still not reading," a voice from outer space replied.
That alien irritated Datner.
"Bring me a tube, size 2.5. And a laryngoscope with a small blade," he practically grumbled, disappointed by the slow flow of the event.
He did not fail to notice that Susan was working flawlessly. With all her faults, she was still quite experienced. She handed him the laryngoscope and the tube.
He put down the Ambu and inserted the laryngoscope.
'Straight up at a right angle. With the patient’s eyes facing the ceiling,' he recalled another piece of advice from Prof. B.S. Advice for all time. A Man for all seasons.
He wondered where B.S. was now.
Probably sitting at home watching TV and getting annoyed about his low salary. Who watches TV at this hour? Is the man a psychopath?!
Never mind. Moving on.
The vocal cords were clearly visible. A piece of cake. He inserted the tube quickly. Now, fixation.
This was the part he hated. He always felt the nurses would cause him to pull out the tube at that moment. Susan, however, didn't panic. "At 9.5 centimeters, Doctor?" she asked, almost affectionately.
"Yes," he mumbled, slightly surprised by her positive approach. He connected the Ambu to the tube and squeezed gently, compressing the small bellows only slightly, so as not to burst the lungs.
Meanwhile, the pulse returned. Approximately.
The monitor showed something that looked approximately like an ECG tracing in Lead 2. Not quite.
The stickers! They had fallen off the baby’s chest. Nurse Miri was attaching them now. Other than that, she was useless. She should learn from Susan.
Pulse 150. A small smile.
"And blood pressure?" Datner almost whispered.
"Wait, I'm changing the cuff, the previous one is too big," Susan answered. He almost began to like her. Not really, but still, a little, given the situation and the alternatives. Better unhinged and efficient than sane and harmful.
Another half a minute passed. Thirty seconds is a long time when you are waiting. He began to remember how tired he was. A big yawn. Overt. For everyone to see. The questionable scent of his breath forced him to stop the show. If you eat something after midnight, it’s best not to have it spicy or with a lot of garlic. Crucially, it's best not to have both ingredients, Datner noted. Failed note.
Meanwhile, the tube fixation was finished, and he turned to adjust the parameters on the ventilator. He never quite understood how to choose the numbers, the ventilation metrics. Strange names for pressures – ‘PIP’, ‘PEEP’, and all sorts of other 'peeps' ran through his head. He also had pressure in his bladder. A sudden need to urinate. Fortunately, he sorted that out relatively easily here. Almost a coincidence. Dumb luck.
"Blood pressure 60/30," Susan cried, almost shouted, in a tone of joy, into the space.
It won't get better than that, Datner decided.
He barely knew what to do with himself now that he was no longer holding the tube or calibrating the ventilator. Nurse Miri smiled. Like a calf that had been given excellent straw.
Nurse Susan was frowning. Despite her advanced age, something of the Southern American beauty in which she had once excelled remained. The Texas beauty queen forty years ago, no doubt. He didn't recall her being originally from New York.
"What about Dextro?" Datner barked.
"Immediately, Doctor," Susan replied submissively. She clearly had excellent training and manners that were out of this world. Foreign to the place.
He almost decided to go out to the stairwell and steal a few puffs of a cigarette. 
Maybe it is better to update the on-call physician first.
But first, read the chart, he concluded.
He knew nothing about the infant who had just returned to life and certainly didn't know why this delicate creature had nearly collapsed completely. The on-call physician would not like a call about resuscitation without concrete information about the patient. He wasn't even sure if it was a male. He thought he saw testes during the ventilation, but he wasn't prepared to swear to it.
Still, a cigarette first. The on-call physician was certainly asleep now, and there was no reason to rush and call her before everything was known.
The watch showed 3:53. Still too symmetrical.
*
"What do you mean, the baby in Room 11 almost died?" the voice on the other end gasped. Datner wasn't sure if Dr. Katya Pavlichuk, the on-call neonatologist, was shouting or talking in her sleep. Maybe it was a combination of both? And what difference did it make anyway?
"He was perfectly fine this morning when I left him," the on-call physician continued, starting to wake up, grumbling about the uninvited wake-up call and the news it brought.
Datner glanced at his watch, 5:15, still symmetrical.
He thought that if he waited long enough, the on-call physician would appreciate the extra sleep time he had allowed her, and it would slightly dull the criticism of his ignorance regarding the chart.
He had tried earlier to read a little in the record, but everything was written in a particularly sloppy handwriting, worse even than his own, and most days there wasn't even a visit note. Only nurses’ comments alongside growth metrics and medication logs.
He gathered it was an infant (it was, after all, a male, those indeed were testes), a 29-week preemie who had been in the NICU for two weeks, receiving some TPN (total parenteral nutrition; nutrition through the vein. The 'T' standing for Total, meaning exclusive IV nutrition, although the baby had already started receiving some formula).
And that was it.
Most of the time, the baby had been idling and lying in the incubator between visits, however many of those were conducted.
This was exactly what the on-call physician, Dr. Katya Pavlichuk, was lecturing him about now.
Datner wasn't really listening. He knew the ways of senior neonatologists. She would dump everything at him, regardless. Better to keep quiet and scowl. Healthier for his coronaries.
After a few more seconds (about two hundred, in Datner's estimation, who had begun to develop a slight, involuntary twitch) of a lecture on the essence of life and the fact that the baby had been perfect that morning when she left, Dr. Katya finally got around to asking something. It sounded like a question. Datner wasn't really listening.
Hello, hello, Datner, are you there?!" Katya shrieked.
"Yes, certainly," Datner replied.
He was entertaining thoughts of early retirement. Considering his age (33, well-balanced), his professional status (a pediatric resident in his third out of four years), and his family status (unhappily married with two daughters who were probably very nice, he didn't really know them), these were premature, idle thoughts.
"How is the baby now? Is he ventilated? Does he need inotropes? Did you take cultures? Did you replace the central line? Did you start antibiotics?" 
This was roughly what Dr. Katya rattled off. Datner wasn't really sure he cared.
"The baby is fine, easily ventilated, no inotropes, and no antibiotics," he replied, trying to avoid revealing the fact that he had failed to insert a central line and hadn't managed to take more than one blood culture. As for urine and cerebrospinal fluid cultures, forget about it. Let the morning shift do that. They rested all night.
He didn't tell Dr. Katya all of that, of course. She hadn't asked specifically. A small, harmless white lie, in Datner's opinion. She said she would arrive in about two hours (funny, that was the usual time for the morning meeting anyway) and that until then, he should update her if there was anything new. Anything at all.
"Yes, of course," Datner answered in an authoritative tone, his thoughts were far less polite.
*
Dr. Katya Pavlichuk thought life was once more beautiful. When she was a child, still in Moscow, she dreamed of becoming a doctor. A pediatrician. She had always been the best student in school, the best student in medical school. Until she arrived in Israel. Straight to 'Sharona'.
When she arrived in the country, they told her 'Sharona' Hospital was in the Sharon region, as the name suggests. 'Two minutes from Tel Aviv,' they said. That was a crude lie; the drive was at least thirty minutes from Tel Aviv, and that was only if you drove at night, with zero traffic. No less. It wasn't really in the Sharon either; it was more in the Coastal Plain. She wasn't sure, and anyway, there was no one to complain to. But that’s where they assigned her, and she, being the good girl she was, did as she was instructed.
That was over twenty years ago already. Like another lifetime.
She tried to feel like she belonged from the start, but they didn't exactly make it easy.
For the first time in her life, she wasn't the popular success. She would hear them mocking her strange accent behind her back. Funny, in her eyes, the Israelis at 'Sharona' had the diction of Orientals. Mongolians. Descendants of Genghis Khan. Almost Mongoloid, she thought, a word she knew she shouldn’t be using. She remembered someone once told her that Dr. Down was a vicious, consummate racist. He was the one who gave the name 'Mongoloid' to babies with three sets of chromosomes 21 and slanted eyes. A smart fellow. A great racist, like all puffed-up Brits, but smart. He probably had crooked teeth. All smart Brits had crooked teeth. Even the not-so-smart ones. And they were all racists.
Only Dr. Renana treated her nicely, back then, when she first arrived at 'Sharona'. They became better friends. Renana was still sometimes happy then. Until that incident.
Now, as a veteran, Katya had learned to live in 'Sharona'. She no longer tried to excel. Excellence at 'Sharona' meant a death blow. A sign on your back. A mark of Cain.
She got out of bed and walked toward the bathroom. That Datner, she thought to herself. Couldn't he have waited another hour before telling her about a deteriorating baby?!
And why was the baby deteriorating anyway? He was perfectly fine this morning.
She would blame Datner for everything at the morning meeting. That was good for his character development. 
The urine flowed relatively easily. In all cases. For Katya, Datner, and the temporarily stabilized preemie.
Relief.
Dr. Katya did not remember to check why the deteriorating baby was not given antibiotic treatment without reason, or what work-up was done to identify the possible infection. It was as if, in the heat of the events, she missed Datner's answer. Too bad; distraction was uncharacteristic of her.
*
Chapter 2  -  A Collection of Amateurs
"A collection of amateurs," I snapped. "Just a bunch of amateurs. Not a single one of them belongs in a professional organization."
The phone rang. It always rings in the bathroom, and always while I’m reading an article about the only soccer team I care about, FC ‘Sharona Sharks.’ A team with no luck; a fan with no luck.
I didn't know who was on the line. I’d replaced too many phones in recent years, and when one of the backups crashed, I just stopped trying to sync contacts. My call log was a graveyard of digits. Most names no longer appeared identified, just numbers, like Holocaust survivors. Those who merited a name, everyone deserves one, after all, were usually labeled as "Blocked," "Do Not Answer," "Do Not Answer 3," or the more recent "Blocked, Do Not Answer Forever. New."
It was Datner. A pleasant enough fellow. I'd known him since he was a young, enthusiastic student. He was a good man, back during his internship. Pediatric residency hadn't done him any favors. His fair hair had receded and turned a premature gray, and his zest for life had almost completely evaporated. He was no longer light-hearted. I’d even known him while he was mourning his mother, and even then, he was more optimistic than he was now.
"Datner, I'm not a consultant for the NICU. Take your madness elsewhere. I had intended to spend the day in glorious, uninterrupted indolence," I shot back before he could even draw breath. Better to set the record straight before the request to claim my soul arrived.
He didn't stop. He was always stubborn. He apologized at length, babbling something incoherent about having been on duty in the NICU three days ago. Now, there were two isolates in a baby’s blood culture. The infectious disease specialist had dismissed it as contamination, but Datner feared it was real. He was truly sorry, he said, but maybe I could take a look?
It sounded like typical nonsense. I told him so. He insisted I come. Even just for five minutes.
I insisted I felt like hell. That was true; I hadn't felt well since the late 1980s. It didn't help. He insisted. The boy was relentless. I told him to shut up and let me drink my coffee, and that I’d be there in fifteen minutes.
"Promise?" he asked. "A sailor's promise, diseased with syphilis," I replied.
He hung up. Slow to take a hint, that one. But a good guy.
*
A few minutes later, I was already nodding my head towards several familiar faces from the past. A gaggle of nurses who I had no idea were still alive. I didn't know any of their names, of course. Except for one, Susan Schell, who stood at the edge of the ward, near the kitchenette. "Is she still alive?" I wondered internally (or perhaps I shouted it, I'm not sure). She hadn't changed much at all. Maybe a wrinkle here, a white hair there, but still the beautiful Susan. An American from hell.
I adopted what I call my 'Dreamy Genius' expression, the one that says 'don't interrupt my profound thoughts' and strode briskly toward the place of the incubator in question, ignoring the astonished gazes of all the occupants. Datner was already standing there, beside the incubator containing a small body and many tubes.
"The little guy doesn't look good, friend," I opened with an immediate taunt.
"Aging fast," the impertinent student replied.
"You were somewhat economical with the truth regarding the patient’s status," I bristled.
"It happened recently, just this morning," Datner tried to defend himself.
A weak, apologetic response. Total surrender.
At this point, I grew tired of the intellectual chess game. More accurately, the easy victory prevented me from feeling any sense of satisfaction, so I decided to get to the point. This way, I would at least significantly cut down on my stay in the NICU, a unit I hadn't tolerated, along with its people, for over sixteen years. I glanced at the patient's chart and even managed to read a few lines before returning to torment Datner. It’s important to arrive prepared for battle; otherwise, there is a danger that the opponent might have a fair chance of success, heaven forbid.
I remember being a young student, not even a resident, when I heard people speaking respectfully about me behind my back. Rumors were circulated about the new genius on the ward, who knew everything during rounds, even before the attending physician. I will reveal the secret of the aforementioned magic to you, even though a proper magician never reveals his secrets. The whole secret lies in arriving half an hour before everyone else, opening all the charts of the new admissions from the night, and memorizing the admission details. Especially numbers of vital signs and selected lab indices. That's it. That’s the whole secret. A little memorization and spurting out the numbers before everyone finishes their coffee, and the title 'genius' is thrown your way without a problem. The art of illusion. The art of the lie.
"So, I see we have a small preemie, ventilated on inotropes, with a borderline pulse and unstable blood pressure, oxygenating with difficulty, and prone to ending his visit on planet Earth. And you say the little prince wasn't like this until your shift?" I fired quickly. That's always my method. Stun them before they regain their composure.
If the fight is fair, there's a good chance you'll lose. After all, I was in enemy territory.
Datner was about to open his mouth when Dr. Katya appeared behind him.
*
"Exactly, Prof. B.S., exactly. Simply appalling. Seventy-two hours ago, this was a completely healthy baby. And now? What a disaster," she almost sobbed. Since when did she get so worked up? I remembered her as a cold fish, not spicy fish stew.
"How are you, dear Dr. Katya?" I mustered my most empathetic tone. I remember not tolerating her 20 years ago, when she first arrived at 'Sharona'. She was already a senior, and I was just a young, clueless resident. This whole meeting felt strange and unwelcome to me.
She didn't answer. She considered making a stinging comment but knew I'd fire back immediately. She gave up. Instead, Datner launched into a speech about cultures. I wasn't listening. There was a medical chart next to the incubator, and I picked it up and saw the problem immediately. I silenced Datner with a finger, and immediately burst forth with the following sentence:
"Gram-positive cocci in chains and Gram-positive bacilli. In the same culture. From the same time. Strange. Definitely strange."
*
"What do you say, Datner? Can you explain to Dr. Pavlichuk and me the possibilities in the differential diagnosis?"
Datner puffed out his chest. It was clear he had prepared for this. He launched into a monologue so long it felt like movie exposition.
"Three big possibilities. All of them are quite strange. First, contamination. The two growths are meaningless. This doesn't explain the child's condition, but it eliminates the need to understand the strange culture result." I smiled; there was an echo of my own words from the past in his reply, it was clear the youth enjoyed quoting me. He continued:
"The second possibility is that only one bacterium is real, and the other is a contaminant. In that case, we need to analyze each possibility regarding each bacterium."
"And the third possibility?" I decided to intervene, even though it was completely unnecessary.
"Both bacteria represent real infections, which are not necessarily related, and may not even have been acquired in the same way, but both led to the child's deterioration." The defense rested.
"I feel almost superfluous here, Datner and Katya. It's clear you've considered all the options. I'm sure you've already discussed the possible identity of the bacteria," I said, injecting a hint of mild insult into my words.
"Of course," Katya shrieked.
That woman needs sedatives; I decreed to myself. I nearly had a heart attack because of her sudden franticness.
"And?" I pressed.
"Datner, tell him," Katya said, with a semblance of quasi-authoritativeness.
It was clear to me that she was afraid of making a mistake, and even more than that, trembling with fear at the possibility that I would correct her.
"The Streptococci are probably GBS," Datner began lecturing, "That's the most common cause of neonatal sepsis, even this late."
"And...?" I continued to press.
"It could also be Enterococcus, though you taught me that without risk factors, it almost never does anything," chirped the visibly unshaven student. This didn't bother me; I had made a point of not arriving clean-shaven at work for over twenty years. I always replied to supervisors' questions about my poor shaving capabilities with the same answer: "When I have time to sleep, I'll shave and maybe even shower." I liked Datner's answer, even though he didn't list every possibility in the world. I decided to let it go and not press the point right now. This was uncharacteristic of me.
"And the second bacterium, Datner?" I continued.
"The second is contamination or Listeria," he answered.
"Excellent," I smiled, "And what about that entire list of Gram-positive bacilli I taught you a million times? Won't you repeat it for me?" I purred sweetly.
"Sure. Listeria, Diphtheroids including Diphtheria, Actinomyces, Nocardia, Clostridium, and something else I forgot," Datner rattled off. I must have taught him that at least two hundred times. Or perhaps I'm exaggerating, and it was only six times..
"You forgot Bacillus, Anthrax, and Cereus," I fired back conspicuously. After all, I had to make it clear there was only one lion in the room.
*

text:
WHY THE WESTERN SIDE OF CHENNAI IS THE BEST DIRECTION FOR CHENNAI’S SECOND AIRPORT

If the Tamil Nadu government is considering Cheyyur, located more than 100 km from Chennai, then other better alternatives at a similar distance should also be seriously examined.

NORTH AND SOUTH OF CHENNAI HAVE MAJOR CONSTRAINTS

NORTHERN SIDE

• Sriharikota and airspace restrictions
• Pulicat Lake and major bird habitats
• Coastal areas vulnerable to severe cyclones and landfalls

SOUTHERN SIDE

• Tambaram airspace considerations
• Kalpakkam security restrictions
• Bird habitats and environmentally sensitive areas
• Coastal belt vulnerable to cyclones, especially during the Northeast Monsoon

These challenges have made airport development in the northern and southern coastal directions increasingly complicated.

WHY THE WESTERN SIDE?

The western side is Chennai’s fastest-growing economic and industrial corridor and offers:

• Outer Ring Road (ORR) connectivity
• Chennai–Bengaluru Highway and Expressway
• Strong existing rail connectivity
• Future ring road and high-speed rail potential
• Rapid industrial and urban growth

Unlike the northern and southern coastal belts, western Chennai provides a strong combination of connectivity, economic growth and long-term development potential.

TWO PRACTICAL ALTERNATIVES

1. EXPAND VELLORE AIRPORT

Vellore already has an operational airport and is undergoing development. With major expansion, it could potentially serve as a larger secondary airport for the wider Chennai region.

2. DEVELOP A GREENFIELD AIRPORT AT PANAPAKKAM

Panapakkam, in Ranipet district, deserves serious consideration due to its strategic location, strong road and rail connectivity, proximity to the Chennai–Bengaluru corridor and access to major industrial clusters.

CONCLUSION

Chennai's second airport should not be chosen based on land availability alone. Distance, accessibility, airspace, environmental concerns, weather risks and long-term economic growth must all be considered.

When all these factors are examined, the western side of Chennai appears to be the most logical direction for long-term airport development.

EXPAND VELLORE AIRPORT OR DEVELOP PANAPAKKAM — BOTH DESERVE SERIOUS CONSIDERATION.

09/06 Saint Zachary, Prophet 
Zechariah, the eleventh of the Twelve Minor Prophets in the Old Testament, began his prophetic ministry around 520 BCE, during the rebuilding of the Second Temple in Jerusalem. As the son of Berechiah and grandson of Iddo, he delivered divine messages through vivid visions and parables, urging the Jewish exiles to repent and remain faithful to God’s covenant. His prophecies, such as the vision of a king entering Jerusalem on a donkey (Zechariah 9:9) and the piercing of a savior (Zechariah 12:10), are seen in Catholic teaching as pointing to the life, passion, and triumph of Jesus Christ. Zechariah’s focus on the Temple’s restoration and God’s enduring promises offered hope, reinforcing the theme that “Yahweh remembers” His covenant. The Catholic Church commemorates him on September 6, honoring his role in salvation history. 
Saint Zachary, pray for us!

text:
Answered here: "1. Where does the Bible say that the Mass is a sacrifice?

Of all of the Catholic doctrines that are denigrated by Fundamentalists as unbiblical, the sacrifice of the Mass has perhaps the most scriptural evidence that Fundamentalists and Catholics are unaware of.

During the Last Supper, the Lord said to his disciples, “Do this in memory of me.” In Greek, this statement reads, “Touto poieite eis tan eman anamnesin.” There are two.aspects of this phrase that deserve consideration. For one, the phrase touto poieite can be translated as do this or as offer this. In the Old Testament, God commands the Israelites “you shall offer (poieseis) upon the altar two lambs” (Ex. 29:38). This use of poiein is translated as offer this or sacrifice this over seventy times in the Old Testament. So the same word that is used for the sacrifice under the Old Covenant is used for the sacrifice of the Mass in the New.

The second key.aspect of this phrase is Our Lord’s use of the word anamnesin. If you were to ask a Protestant to look in a Greek Translation of his Bible, every time this word (anamnesis) appears it is within a sacrificial context (see, for example, Numbers 10:10). It also can be translated as memorial offering or memorial sacrifice. While these nuances are lost in the English translation, Jewish ears would have understood the sacrificial meaning of Christ’s words.

Another New Testament passage that testifies to the sacrificial nature of the Mass is 1 Corinthians 10:14–21. Here Paul argues that participation in the Lord’s table means refusing to participate in the sacrifices of demons. Paul contrasts two groups: The first are those who participate in one altar (the table of demons), eating the sacrifice and drinking from the cup of demons. The second are those who partake of the table of the Lord (which, according to Malachi 1:7 is synonymous with an altar of sacrifice) and drink from the cup of the Lord. Paul’s argument is based upon the parallelism between the demonic sacrifice and the Christian sacrifice. Hebrews 13:10 follows this thought, saying that we have an altar from which those who serve the tent (Jewish priests serving in the temple) have no right to eat."

text:
Northern Purification of the Southern Murugan — Editorial Explained

Introduction

Devdutt Pattanaik’s article offers a fascinating exploration of Murugan, revealing how Indian religious traditions evolved through cultural interaction, assimilation and reinterpretation, rather than through rigid regional boundaries.

1. Who is Murugan?

Murugan is a major Tamil deity associated with youth, beauty, warfare, mountains and fertility.

In wider Sanskritic tradition, he is identified with Kartikeya/Skanda, the son of Shiva and Parvati and commander of the divine army.

The article highlights that multiple traditions developed around this deity, sometimes with significantly different narratives.

2. What does “Northern Purification” mean?

The phrase refers to the gradual incorporation of a Southern/local deity into the broader Sanskritic religious imagination.

Local traditions were not necessarily erased. Instead, they were often:

Reinterpreted through Sanskritic mythology

Connected with Puranic narratives

Incorporated into temple institutions

Given pan-Indian identities.

This reflects Sanskritisation and cultural acculturation, but also demonstrates that influence was interactive rather than purely one-way.

3. North–South cultural synthesis

The fascinating point is that Murugan remained deeply Tamil in cultural expression, even while becoming identified with the pan-Indian Skanda/Kartikeya.

Practices such as Kavadi, hill worship and stories of Valli preserve distinctive Southern traditions.

Thus:

Regional deity → Cultural interaction → Sanskritic reinterpretation → Pan-Indian religious identity

4. Broader civilisational lesson

The article challenges simplistic binaries such as “North versus South” or “local versus Sanskritic.”

Indian civilisation has historically developed through pluralism, syncretism, adaptation and negotiation among diverse traditions—including Brahminical, Buddhist, Jain and indigenous practices.

Conclusion

Murugan’s transformation demonstrates that Indian unity has often been constructed through accommodation of diversity rather than elimination of difference. Cultural identities can simultaneously remain regional and become part of a wider civilisational consciousness.

UPSC Keywords

Sanskritisation | Syncretism | Cultural Assimilation | Acculturation | Religious Pluralism | Regional Identity | Cultural Integration | Civilisational Continuity | North–South Interface

text:
A few thoughts on capital and a home.

When you had it easy as a kid—doctor dad, mom nurse, fancy prep school where you study Latin, et al—it’s hard to develop killer instincts towards keeping gains. I think the killer traders are the ones who know hard times and who really appreciate money.

I have made, and then given back, life-changing gains on more than one occasion. So dumb.

Although my means and income are modest, I never really appreciated the value of money. Easy come, easy go. I had my books and records, cats and speakers, a rental apartment—it’s fine.

Last year I went on a killer run with precious metals. Closing my final calls on the day of the highs and then shorting silver to oblivion, which felt a little rude.

Unlike the insane ai trades which I recently round-tripped, I vowed to keep my gold and silver spoils and trade them for a home.

I found an unbelievable property in Kamakura on temple lands.

Temples never sell their land and often own the land entire nearby neighborhoods are built on. They make income by leasing their lands to homeowners.

Instead of buying the land, you buy the rights to a 20-year lease which you can renew. Since you don’t pay land tax, the price difference is not that large in the end.

But these land-lease properties tend to list 30% below market price because one, the lease adds up over decades, and two, you cannot get loans for them basically. Banks can confiscate the house but not the land if you default.

This creates opportunity. The buying pool is limited to cash buyers. An agent knew I was a cash buyer looking for something unique so he contacted me about a property that was about to be listed.

I visited, in awe, and next day submitted a formal offer, with dreams so high I could only assume they would be dashed.

A trader would argue for capital efficiency—why give up all that capital when mortgage rates in Japan are so low? But the decision was easy. I value mental efficiency. After living in a rented apartment for decades and trading from the noisy kitchen table or even noisier phone, the mental efficiency of a house fully paid for dwarfs all.

My long-suffering wife and long-lived cats now have their own castle, their own garden, on holy temple lands.

Seeing my cats touch grass for the first time, exploring their new territory with excitement and trepidation, is so precious. Next year they will meet a puppy for the first time. I expect trepidation outweighs in that round…

The portfolio account is small again but that’s fine. I robbed a bullion bank once—I know I can rob one again. And I know where all this is going. It’s simply a matter of time.

So I’m timing the movement of the guards with my stopwatch. Ready for Heat again.

And on this first Sunday I woke up to temple meditation bells. A few minutes early? Late?

My new form of time-being that was always there, just waiting for me to arrive and hear.
